§9.3.3 Multi-Row Header Tiers

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-multi-row-header-tiers · tables headers encoding

✅ Normative

Every printed header tier MUST be rendered as its own header row, with exact colspans. A group header MUST span only its data columns; the row-label stub takes a rowspan across the header rows instead.

Printed:  |            BI          |            PD          |
          | Indicated  | Proposed  | Indicated  | Proposed  |

Every real tier is kept

Both rows are rendered with their spans — [colspan=2]BI over Indicated | Proposed, and so on.

The stack MUST NOT be flattened into one row of concatenated labels: "BI Indicated", "BI Proposed" is non-conforming, not a stylistic choice. It destroys the grouping that the page printed and makes the number of header rows depend on the producer rather than the page.

A wrapped parent phrase is still a tier. "(Paid as of 12-31-2020)" broken across two lines and spanning its sub-columns is a genuine tier — "it wrapped" does not demote it. The span, not the line count, decides; Header Wrap vs Real Tier§9.3.2 has the full test.

The group header stops at the first data column

A group super-header spans its data columns and never the row-label stub. The stub takes a rowspan across the header rows:

<th rowspan="2">UW Category</th><th colspan="3">Inception to Date</th>
<!-- then: -->  Earned Premium | Incurred Claims | Loss Ratio

The group's colspan MUST equal its leaf count, exactly.

The printed rule under the group starts at the first data column. The stub is not part of "Inception to Date" — the stub says which row, the group says which measure. Different axes, so they do not share a span. Spanning the stub as well is the most common way this goes wrong.

Reconciling the tracks

The leaf-column tracks N of the table are counted. For each header row, the expanded colspans, occupied plus explicit blank tracks, MUST add up to N.

A mismatch shows which kind of error was made, before anything else is inspected:

  1. a missed column
  2. a wrong span
  3. two tables fused into one
  4. a header line read as the wrong kind of thing

Period stacks in financial statements

| $ in millions |       Average for the        |  ← corner note; apex tier
|               | Three Months Ended | Year …  |
|               | December | December | Dec…   |  ← stacked "December"/"2024"
|               | 2024     | 2023     | 2024   |    is ONE leaf label

Period headers follow the same rules, with a few fixed calls of their own — apex qualifiers, stacked month-over-year labels and the "$ in millions" corner note. They are set out in SEC Period Tiers§9.3.4, which governs 10-K and 10-Q header stacks.
